caption:
Ebola cases surge to 676 in DRC, outbreak worsens

The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported 676 confirmed cases, 136 deaths, and 119 suspected cases as of June 11. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebolavirus, is the third largest Ebola outbreak on record.

Health experts fear the outbreak could grow much larger and had been quietly spreading for months before the outbreak was declared on May 15. Investigators are working backward to find the first case—patient zero—and have identified a possible early superspreader event on February 4.

The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention released modeling of how the outbreak could unfold, warning that if public health interventions aren’t implemented swiftly and strongly, the outbreak could rival or exceed the largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded.

The Trump administration’s isolationist strategy involving travel restrictions and border closures has raised tensions in other countries, including Kenya, where protesters have gathered to oppose plans for a makeshift quarantine facility at a military base.
